headline: GOLD OPENS AT $4,074 AND SILVER AT $58.65 ON IRAN TALKS PAUSE — Fed Holds 5.5% But September Hike At 67% Probability; Precious Metals Bid Returns
snippet: Gold futures opened at approximately $4,074/oz on Monday August 3, 2026 — up from Friday's close — and silver September futures opened at $58.65/oz (spot $58.22), up 1.10%, as President Trump announced a second consecutive weekend pause on planned Iran airstrikes, lifting precious metals on renewed safe-haven demand. The Federal Reserve held rates at 5.50% at its July 30 meeting in a 9-3 vote, with three hawkish governors dissenting in favour of an immediate hike; Fed Funds futures now price a 67% probability of a September increase, maintaining the monetary uncertainty backdrop that has pushed gold up over 30% year-to-date. OPEC+ simultaneously approved an additional 188,000 bpd supply increase that sent oil prices sharply lower, reinforcing gold's defensive appeal heading into US non-farm payrolls data later in the week.

headline: BENZ MINING HITS 41m AT 14.5 G/T AU AT ICON, GLENBURGH — Three High-Grade Intercepts From New NE-Plunging Hinge Zones; Maiden JORC Resource H1 2027 (ASX/TSX-V: BNZ/BZ)
source_name: Investing News Network / Benz Mining Corp
snippet: Benz Mining Corp (ASX: BNZ, TSX-V: BZ) reported August 2, 2026 that drilling at the Icon Zone of its Glenburgh Gold Project in Western Australia returned 41 metres at 14.5 g/t gold alongside 75 metres at 2.3 g/t and 39 metres at 3.6 g/t — all from newly identified northeast-plunging hinge zones that represent a structural discovery substantially expanding the known geometry of the deposit. The results confirm a system open along multiple orientations, with each new hinge zone discovery adding incremental resource potential to a project already demonstrating bulk-tonnage grade continuity; a maiden JORC resource estimate is targeted for H1 2027. Glenburgh is one of the more compelling near-term resource definition stories among Australian gold explorers, sitting in a proven gold district at a moment when gold in AUD terms is above A$6,400/oz.

headline: ANGLOGOLD ASHANTI Q2: HEADLINE EARNINGS UP 58% TO $1B, $2B EBITDA, $727M FREE CASH FLOW — Swings From $311M Net Debt To $991M Net Cash; 72-Cent Dividend (NYSE: AU)
snippet: AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) delivered its strongest Q2 on record by most financial metrics on August 1, 2026 — headline earnings up 58% year-over-year to $1 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 46% to $2 billion, and free cash flow of $727 million on 744,000 oz sold at an average realized price of $4,446/oz. The balance sheet transformation is equally notable: the group swung from $311 million net debt a year ago to $991 million net cash, enabled in part by the April 16 repurchase of $666 million in bonds. AngloGold declared a 72-cent Q2 interim dividend, and Q2 gold production of 744,000 oz was roughly 7% below the prior-year period — meaning the price environment more than offset volume softness in every financial metric that matters to investors.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q2: RECORD $3.5B H1 CASH FLOW AND $625M RETURNED TO SHAREHOLDERS — Barnat Pit Wall Collapse Locks 370,000 oz Through 2028; Full-Year Guidance Toward Low End (NYSE: AEM)
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (NYSE: AEM, TSX: AEM) reported July 30, 2026 that H1 2026 operating cash flow reached a record $3.5 billion, with Q2 gold production of 856,000 oz and $625 million returned to shareholders via dividends and buybacks — but the headline is a July 1 rock wall movement at the Barnat open pit in Quebec that has locked approximately 370,000 oz of gold inaccessible through 2028, reducing H2 2026 production by 60,000–80,000 oz and weighing on the 2027–28 mine plan. The company maintained its full-year guidance range of 3.3–3.5 million oz but flagged the lower end as more likely. Adjusted EPS of $3.07 narrowly missed the $3.10 consensus. For investors in Canadian gold juniors in Quebec, the Barnat incident is a reminder of rock mechanics risk in open-pit operations and how quickly a single operational event can shift a major's production profile.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER Q2: RECORD $354M ADJUSTED EBITDA AND $739.7M REVENUE — Seventh Consecutive Record Quarter As Realized Copper Hits US$6.22/lb (TSX: CS, ASX: CSC)
snippet: Capstone Copper Corp (TSX: CS, ASX: CSC) reported Q2 2026 results on July 30 showing record adjusted EBITDA of $354 million and record revenue of $739.7 million — up 36% year-over-year — marking the seventh consecutive quarter of record financial performance, driven by a realized copper price of US$6.22/lb and continued throughput improvements at its Mantoverde and Santo Domingo operations in Chile. The result cements Capstone as one of the highest-margin pure-play copper producers on the TSX at a moment when copper has risen over 45% year-over-year, generating a cash flow base that supports accelerated organic growth investment in H2 2026. For investors tracking copper developer valuations, Capstone's margin profile at $6.22/lb realized is an important benchmark when stress-testing NAV models.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SILVER Q2: RECORD $416M REVENUE (+53% YOY) AND $252M EBITDA (+110%) — Silver Price Breakout Drives Best Quarter In Company History (TSX: FR)
snippet: First Majestic Silver Corp (TSX: FR, NYSE: AG) reported July 30, 2026 that Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $416 million — up 53% year-over-year — with adjusted EBITDA of $252 million, up 110%, marking the best financial quarter in the company's 24-year history as the silver price averaged well above $55/oz during the period. Cash flow generation in H1 2026 alone has exceeded the company's full-year 2024 free cash flow, illustrating the operating leverage that primary silver producers carry at current price levels. Operational challenges at certain mines were flagged on the earnings call but were more than offset by the silver price tailwind — a dynamic that makes First Majestic the sector bellwether investors should reference when sizing silver royalty and exploration positions.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING TRANSFERS U.S. LISTING TO NASDAQ GLOBAL SELECT MARKET AUGUST 11 — Higher-Tier Exchange Move Targets Institutional Flow; Colombia Gold-Copper-Silver Focus (TSX: CNL)
source_name: Investing News Network / Collective Mining Ltd
snippet: Collective Mining Ltd (TSX: CNL, NYSE American: CNL) announced it will voluntarily transfer its U.S. listing from NYSE American to the Nasdaq Global Select Market effective August 11, 2026, retaining the CNL ticker — a move to a higher-tier venue with stricter listing standards that typically signals management confidence in balance sheet and operational trajectory. The TSX listing and CUSIP are unchanged. Collective Mining is advancing a gold-silver-copper-tungsten discovery in Caldas, Colombia; the Nasdaq upgrade broadens the institutional investor universe that can access the stock and may improve analyst coverage. For junior investors tracking Colombia exploration, this is a structural positive for the company's capital markets profile.

headline: MINERAL RESOURCES RESTARTS BALD HILL LITHIUM MINE AFTER 18-MONTH PAUSE — First Shipments Q1 FY27; A$20M Capex; 58.1Mt Resource At 0.9% Li2O (ASX: MIN)
snippet: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) has restarted its 100%-owned Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia after placing it on care and maintenance in November 2024 when lithium prices collapsed below operating cost — with crushing and mining resuming in June 2026, first concentrate produced in July, and first shipments through the Port of Esperance targeted for Q1 FY27. Restart capital expenditure is estimated at approximately A$20 million, modest against a 58.1 million tonne resource at 0.9% Li2O. Full FY27 guidance including sales volumes, FOB costs, and total capex is expected August 27, 2026. The restart is a direct signal from management that the current lithium price environment — with lithium carbonate up ~96% year-over-year despite recent softness — justifies returning idled Australian hard-rock supply to market.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM Q2 2026: 35,000t PRODUCED AT GROTA DO CIRILO, 6% BEAT ON GUIDANCE — Full Financial Results August 14; Operations Upgrade Successful (Nasdaq: SGML)
snippet: Sigma Lithium (Nasdaq: SGML) produced 35,000 tonnes of high-grade spodumene concentrate at its Grota do Cirilo project in Minas Gerais, Brazil in Q2 2026 — beating its own production guidance of approximately 33,000 tonnes by roughly 6% — following a successful mining operations upgrade that management says has sustainably improved throughput. Full Q2 2026 financial and operating results are scheduled for release August 14, 2026. The production beat reinforces Sigma's position as one of the few operating ex-China hard-rock lithium producers reporting results in line with or ahead of plan, a distinction that carries increasing weight as institutional capital discriminates between lithium producers on execution track record.

headline: DRC COBALT EXPORT QUOTA SET AT 96,600t IN 2026 — Half Of Prior-Year Output Drives Cobalt Toward ~$58,000/t; Sixth Consecutive Deficit Year Forecast (Benchmark Minerals)
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo's 2026 cobalt export quota is set at 96,600 tonnes — approximately half of the country's 2024 production volume of over 200,000 metric tonnes — with 87,000t allocated pro rata to existing producers and 9,600t under discretionary control, a supply constraint that has pushed cobalt prices to approximately $58,000 per metric tonne in H1 2026, more than tripling from prior-year lows. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and Wood Mackenzie both project the global cobalt market is entering structural deficit, with secondary (recycled) cobalt supply growing 43% in 2026 following China's August 2025 lifting of its ban on black mass imports only partially offsetting quota-driven tightness. The DRC quota regime is the single most important supply-side variable for cobalt-exposed battery metals investors tracking the critical minerals investment cycle.
